Marco — thanks, and good questions. High level answers first; I'll attach a short draft TIA bridge we typically use for customers that need SCCs + UK addendum.

1) Processing locations: by default hosted requests may be routed through EU regions; we maintain control-plane in the US but persistent storage and inference for EU customers can be pinned to EU-only clusters under Redwood Private or Dedicated. Transient runtime elements (e.g., batching & KV caches) may touch GPU nodes in the requested region; we don't persist KV caches beyond session TTLs unless the customer opts into fine-tuned cache features.

2) SCCs + UK Addendum: we provide a bundle (SCC annex + UK Addendum) as a consolidated package for enterprise customers — single attachment you can review. If you need separate instruments that's doable but adds admin overhead.

3) TIA / DTIA coverage: we maintain an internal TIA that documents data pathways for cross-border flows and the categories of subprocessors. The TIA explicitly calls out CDN, metrics pipeline, and log storage as subprocessors with onshore/offshore options. For highly regulated customers we can scope-out certain subprocessors (e.g., exclude cloud analytics) or enable region-locking on Dedicated/Private.

Next steps:
- I'll ask Kimberly (Legal ops) to validate the bridge wording vs. our standard UK addendum.
- Naomi (Privacy) will populate the subprocessor table and provide the evidence snapshot (SOC2 control references and encryption attestations).
- I will return a consolidated response and a draft redwood-tia-bridge-draft.docx by Monday (Nov 30).

Jonas
Senior Manager, Trust & Privacy — Redwood Inference
